name: Build-to-rent — attached/horizontal
summary: Single-owner rental communities of attached townhomes, duplex/cottage clusters or one-story 'horizontal apartments', with private drives and an amenity center. Cost sits between for-sale townhomes and garden apartments: shared walls and compact 1–3 bedroom plans, but every unit has its own ground-floor entry, roof and often a yard. Per NAHB's 2016 profile, 77% of single-family built-for-rent homes were attached. The only cost line-items found are an illustrative 2026 Sun Belt BTR townhome pro forma and NAHB's community-level capitalization figure, so the default is derived from the townhomes file. Confidence is low-medium.

typicalSize.method: The pro forma example is 48 units (e1); NAHB cites a typical 200-unit BTR project (btr-detached e1). Horizontal-apartment communities commonly run 120–250 units. Judgment.

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: The pro forma's 3-bed BTR townhomes average 1,350 SF (e1). Single-story horizontal apartments (1–2 bed) run ~700–1,100 SF. The 2016 SFBFR median was 1,500 SF (btr-detached e4). Mid 1,200 SF blends townhome and cottage product.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Horizontal apartments and attached BTR typically run ~10–15 units per gross acre, between detached BTR (~6.5) and garden apartments (~20+). Judgment.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Surface stalls/carports for horizontal apartments; attached-garage townhomes at the high end. Judgment.

perPrimaryUnit.method: = perSF × sfPerPrimaryUnit (incl. horizontal share): mid $190 × 1,200 = $228k; low $150 × 1,000 = $150k; high $240 × 1,400 = $336k. Anchor: the 2026 Sun Belt BTR townhome pro forma (e1) shows vertical $165/SF × 1,350 SF = $222.8k plus horizontal $35k = $257.8k/unit, i.e. $191/SF all-in hard. The for-sale townhomes file (mid $150/SF vertical, 2025$) plus ~$30k/unit horizontal gives $150 × 1,200 + 30k = $210k ($175/SF). Mid $190/SF follows the pro forma. Labeled 2026$.

perSF.method: All-in hard per unit SF incl. horizontal infrastructure. Mid ≈ the e1 pro forma ($257.8k / 1,350 SF = $191). Low = townhome low ($115) + horizontal (~$30/SF) ≈ $145–150. High = premium/high-cost-region townhome ($200) + horizontal ($40) = $240.

scope.notes: Buildings plus in-community horizontal work (private drives, parking, wet/dry utilities, stormwater, landscaping, fencing) incl. GC general conditions and OH&P. Excludes the amenity center (line item), land, off-sites, impact/tap fees, soft costs and FF&E.

systemSplit.method: The townhomes split is scaled to ~86% for the buildings. The ~14% horizontal share ($35k of $258k in e1) goes to 31 (grading), 32 (drives, parking, landscape, fencing) and 33 (utilities). Div 21 covers sprinklers where buildings exceed IRC limits.

cost.method: The e1 pro forma carries $35k/door for 'lot development and infrastructure'. Mid is set lower at $30k for the higher density of horizontal apartments; the range is judgment.

lineItems.name: Amenity center: clubhouse/leasing, pool, dog park

cost.method: Judgment, same build-up as btr-detached (clubhouse ~$300/SF, pool, dog park, mail kiosk), slightly smaller for denser product.

lineItems.notes: Added on top of the per-unit hard cost.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Judgment: window coverings, smart-home kits and the clubhouse furniture share. Appliances are in the hard cost.

pctOfHard.method: The e1 pro forma uses soft costs at 13% of hard plus carry/interest reserve at 5.5% of total project cost. Mid 17% includes financing fees and lease-up marketing on top of the 13%. | Second pass (2026-10-24, main session): Reduced 2 points to remove financing fees the mid added. The engine adds impact & tap fees, the developer fee and construction financing as their own lines (docs/BUDGET_ENGINE.md §5), so this bucket must exclude them.

softCosts.notes: Interest reserve may be modeled separately via the financing norms.

hard.method: The e1 pro forma carries 'Contingency (8% of hard cost)'; that is the mid. Low/high is judgment.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Low $150k × 1.12 ≈ $168k; high $335k × 1.24 + amenity share ≈ $430k, rounded. The e1 pro forma total of $383k/door includes $50k land, so it sits at ~$333k excluding land.

evidence.quote: Vertical hard costs $10.69M ($165/SF); Horizontal/site (lot development and infrastructure) $1.68M [$35K per door]; Total project cost $18.41M [$383K per door]
evidence.scopeNotes: Illustrative 48-unit, 1,350 SF average 3-bed BTR townhome pro forma (May 2026), not an actual project. Land $2.4M ($50K/door); soft costs 13% of hard; contingency 8% of hard; carry/interest 5.5% of total project cost. 'Sun Belt' is mapped to US because no market is specified.

openQuestions: Only one cost line-item source (illustrative). Public budgets for horizontal-apartment communities (e.g., NexMetro/Avilla, Christopher Todd) in city incentive or PID filings would materially improve this.
Unit-size mix (cottage flats vs 3-bed townhomes) moves per-unit cost ±30%; the engine may want a unit-mix input.
